I'm not a career politician. I don't come from a political family. 

But I promised to fight for ALL Marylanders, and that's exactly what we did this session. Here's what we got done. ⬇️

Video

The beautiful environment we have – it's our job to protect it, just like we’d do with any heirloom.

Protect it. Care for it. And hopefully pass on something just as beautiful as the way that you found it.

Video

Hitting our land conservation goal SIX years early, planting five MILLION trees across the state, working in partnership to turn underdeveloped land and crumbling apartments into affordable homes near Metro and light rail stations, supporting farmers and ensuring cleaner water for our Bay. 

Every day, our administration is putting in the work to protect our land, water, and people. Happy Earth Day, Maryland.

Honored to have visited @StMarysMD — our state's public honors college and a top-five ranked liberal arts college in the nation.

Students chose this college, the College's leadership has delivered on their success, and our latest budget backs that up with a $2 million operating increase and funding to renovate Montgomery Hall.

🎉 Congrats to the EIGHT Maryland students who will be playing with NYO-USA this summer!

We’re proud of each of you and know you’ll represent our state with pride.

Henry Golden (Bethesda) – Apprentice Composer,
Jacqi Fan (Ellicott City) – Violin, 
Samuel Lee (Laurel) – Bassoon,
Isaac Won (Potomac) – Trumpet,
Bakari Lyons (Woodlawn) – Violin,
Chloe Robertson (Rockville) – Violin,
Erin Yi (Ashton) – Viola, and
Donna Lee (Clarksburg) – Timpani & Percussion.

Charlotte Hall Veterans Home is Maryland's only state-operated veterans home.

When we took office, it was in a state of complete disrepair and decay, and had a 1-Star rating.

We ended the contract with the previous operator, and our Board of Public Works brought in a new operator.

Now, Charlotte Hall has a 4-Star overall rating.

Video

When we took office, Charlotte Hall Veterans Home was in a state of complete disrepair and decay, and had a 1-Star rating from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.

So we took action. We ended the contract with the previous operator, and our Board of Public Works approved an emergency contract to bring in a new operator.

Now, Charlotte Hall has a 4-Star overall rating.

Sen. Simonaire, thank you for your 20 years of service to our state. You’ve been a great partner in the work of making Maryland a better state, and I’ve deeply appreciated your advocacy for educators and our military community.

But here in Maryland, we’re going to keep investing in our people.

Thanks again to the students and staff at Fort Washington Forest Elementary!

This year has been exceptionally hard on Marylanders with the attacks from the Trump-Vance administration. 

We used this legislative session to help those impacted, delivering results that help Marylanders with housing, employment, government assistance, utility costs, and more. 

We are pushing back against the federal government and continuing to push forward for the people of our state.

As the first point of contact for emergencies, 911 specialists provide an invaluable service to the public and help keep our first responders informed and prepared. 

Here in Maryland, we’ve created the Commission to Advance Next Generation 9-1-1 and have worked across the aisle to pass laws that give these heroes the support they need – both on and off the job. 

They’re true life-savers, and I cannot thank them enough for their dedication to leaving no one behind.

BREAKING:

Today, a federal court granted a preliminary injunction halting construction on the proposed ICE Facility in Washington County.

This ruling is a major and welcome step forward. We’ve been clear from the start: this project raises grave concerns for Washington County — from environmental damage, to water and sewer capacity, to emergency services, to the loss of economic opportunity, to the broader lack of transparency around this process. The courage of Marylanders changes and saves lives. 

I am proud to sign the Vax Act and the Jillian and Lindsay Wiener Short-Term Rental Safety Act into law.

Video
At a time when costs are rising, Maryland is taking steps to help families make ends meet and help more people lead healthier lives.

This is a big day for the ARLIS team and for the future of quantum.

The future of job growth, wealth creation, and economic prosperity is quantum. That’s why in Maryland, we want to be the global capital of quantum computing.

For decades, we’ve had the right assets to lead in this area, but we had NO strategy to do so. 

Now we're asset-rich and strategy-aligned. In three years, we've attracted more than $10 BILLION in private investment to the state.

In Maryland, we don't play for second pla

Maryland’s vaccine policy will be led by science – not internet conspiracy theories.

We will protect our people, no matter how they voted in the last election.

The Vax Act decouples the state’s vaccine authority from the federal government. Our vaccine policy will be led by science – not internet conspiracy theories.

The Jillian and Lindsay Wiener Short-Term Rental Safety Act – sponsored by Delegate Foley and Senator Feldman – requires fire detection and prevention equipment in every short-term rental, mandates annual inspections, and ensures accountability.
